newsitem.title: DENMARK: Foreign investors help Danish bonds upwards.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investors help Danish bonds upwards.

text.p: Danish bond prices climbed in a positive market on Tuesday buoyed by solid foreign investor participation with dealers seeing prices stabilising at current levels for the rest of the day.

"The market undertone is really strong with foreign investors in particular buying a lot of local paper. Prices have probably peaked for today, but they should keep to current levels up to the close," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was 0.26 point up from the opening at 111.96, yielding 6.23 percent in turnover of 3.1 billion crowns.

The 2006 benchmark was forecast to trade within the 111.90-112.15 range for the rest of the day. Its March future rose 0.52 point to 111.70 with 250 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.20 point to 88.90.
The crown traded at 3.8107 per mark at 1140 gmt, up very marginally from around 3.8110 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one basis point to 65 during the course of the morning.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling short-term state bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
